BiblicalUsage: Chamush describes men harnessed for battle, arrayed by fives, and it marks Israel on the move. God led the children of Israel out of Egypt harnessed, the armed men of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh passed before their brethren into the land, and they crossed the Jordan harnessed before the LORD. Gideon, told to go down to the host, heard the enemy talking in their camp.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word shows that Israel did not wander unarmed into the promise: God ordered them like an army, five by five, before they had fought a single battle. I hold that readiness is part of faith, and the crossing of the Jordan proves it.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea; Crossing the Jordan
